First development release of 0.19.0: a Lifecycle page for every end date, an applications catalog with installed software per device, cooling modelled alongside power from the plant down to each device's intake, application flows with an exportable diagram, software target versions with a compliance check, the first fixes for the bugs reported against 0.18.1, and the leftovers from 0.18.1.

> [!CAUTION]
> **This is a development release. It is not stable and it contains bugs.** Do not run it in production or on data you can't restore. Take a backup before upgrading a test install, and expect behaviour to change before 0.19.0. If you run into a problem, please [submit a bug report](https://github.com/danbyte-net/danbyte/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) - every report helps get 0.19.0 right.

> [!NOTE]
> **Behaviour changes:**
> - **A deactivated tenant's Outposts and syncs stop.** An Outpost token of a deactivated tenant is refused on every Outpost endpoint and on the build download, its SSH Outposts are no longer driven, and its Windows, virtualization and Zabbix connections are no longer synced; a job queued before the deactivation returns without running.
> - **Rack placement checks cooling.** A rack with a cooling capability refuses liquid, hybrid or immersion hardware it does not take. Air-cooled gear goes in any rack, and racks without a capability take anything.
> - **Time bars colour by time left** against the warning window, not by percent used.
> - **List endpoints answer 100 rows by default.** A request without `page_size` now returns 100 rows and a `next` link instead of up to 10,000; pass `page_size` (up to 10,000) or follow `next`. The web app does this itself. API scripts that read a whole list without paging must add `page_size` or follow `next`.
> - **Site roles gain the new types.** Existing site viewer and editor roles are upgraded to cover cooling sources, feeds, intakes and outflows, installed software and the applications catalog, the same way the 0.18 upgrade handled support coverage.

### Lifecycle

- #436 - **One time bar for every end date.** Hardware, OS and support coverage bars now colour by time left against their warning window instead of by percent used. The OS bar uses the platform's entered dates or, failing those, its endoflife.date cycle, and the tooltip says which. VMs get an OS support row and the device's Support coverage row gets the bar.
- #436 - **Lifecycle page.** DCIM → Devices → Lifecycle lists every device and VM against its hardware, OS and coverage end dates, soonest first. It has window count chips, facets, deep links (`/lifecycle?source=coverage&window=90`), export and its own saved views; the data comes from `GET /api/lifecycle/`.
- #436 - **Next end of life column.** The Devices and Virtual machines lists offer an optional column with each object's soonest end and its source, sorted by days left.
- #436 - **Applications catalog.** A new Applications list under DCIM → Devices records the software you run, nested into a domain → process → application tree, with an optional endoflife.date product.
- #436 - **Installed software.** Device and VM pages get a Software tab recording each application and version. Cycles follow the version, and import, export and the API cover it. The application page's Installed on tab has an Add button that records the application on a device or VM from there.
- #436 - **Software on the Lifecycle page.** Installed software is the fourth source on the Lifecycle page and counts toward Next end of life.
- #436 - **Compliance includes software.** End-of-life status rules can opt in to failing a device or VM on its installed software; existing rules are unchanged.
- #395 - **Software target.** Platforms take a target version and devices and VMs a software version; the overview shows "17.9.4a · target 17.9.5", and device and VM lists gain Software version and Target columns with a Software target filter.
- #395 - **Software target compliance check.** A new check fails devices and VMs that run something other than their platform's target version, with "Running 17.9.4a, target 17.9.5" as the reason; optionally a missing version fails too.
- #395 - **ESXi version from vCenter.** With Read host hardware on, the vCenter sync fills each host's software version (e.g. 8.0.3) and keeps it current, without overwriting a version typed by hand.

### Application flows

- #163 - **Application flows.** Record the traffic an application needs, from an address, range, prefix or any to another, by protocol and ports, with a status and direction. Flows tabs on applications, devices, VMs, IP addresses and prefixes list them, including flows to prefixes and ranges that hold the object's addresses.
- #163 - **Flow diagram and export.** The application's Diagram tab draws its flows left to right with arrowed lines labelled like "TCP 443". It exports as PNG, SVG, PDF or draw.io, or prints.

### Cooling

- #434 - **Cooling on hardware and racks.** Device types, module types and devices record how they're cooled (air, liquid, hybrid, immersion), and device types record their heat output. Racks and rack types record what their cooling takes and how much heat it removes. A rack refuses hardware its cooling doesn't take, and lists devices placed before it was made stricter.
- #434 - **Heat load against cooling capacity.** Racks add up their devices' heat (the type's heat output, else the power drawn, PDUs aside) against cooling capacity. It shows on the rack page, the racks list's Cooling column, floor plans coloured by Cooling, the tile popover, the 3D rack card and the site Capacity tab. Rack and device lists filter by capability, free cooling, method and mismatch.
- #434 - **Airflow from the API, power budget on rack types.** The device and device-type forms read airflow from `/api/dcim/choices/`; the device page shows its effective airflow and the type page its own. Rack types carry a power budget that the rack form pre-fills, Sync type copies and the rack-type import reads.
- #434 - **Cooling sources and feeds.** Model the cooling plant like power: units such as chillers, CRAHs and in-row coolers in a site, and loops to racks carrying rated capacity, flow and supply/return temperatures, with lists, bulk edit and delete, import/export and a rack's Cooling feeds tab.
- #434 - **Cooling capacity from feeds.** A rack without its own cooling capacity is measured against what its primary cooling feeds deliver, and each feed and source shows the heat it carries against its rating.
- #434 - **What a source takes down.** Power panels and feeds and cooling sources and feeds get an Affected tab listing the racks and devices downstream as outage or reduced redundancy, and Plan maintenance opens an event with those impacts filled in.
- #434 - **Cooling sources on floor plans.** A floor-plan tile can link to a cooling source, and its popover shows the source's load against its rating. The sidebar's Power section is now "Power & cooling".
- #434 - **Cooling intakes and outflows.** Devices and device types gain cooling intakes and outflows, with connector, diameter and max flow. An intake takes coolant from a feed or from a CDU's outflow, and templates stamp them onto new devices and travel in bundles.
- #434 - **Cooling path.** The device overview shows each intake's path from source through any CDU, also served at `/api/devices/{id}/cooling-path/`.
- #434 - **Connected feed load and flow.** Where intakes name a feed, its load is the heat of the devices they connect, and its Loop card shows their summed flow against the feed's own. The Affected tab follows intakes and shows each device's path.
- #434 - **Unconnected liquid hardware.** A liquid, hybrid or immersion rack's Devices tab filters liquid-cooled devices with no intake connected (`?cooling_unconnected=1`).

### Fixed

- #447 - **Smaller default page on list endpoints.** A list request without `page_size` now returns 100 rows (`API_PAGE_SIZE`) with a `next` link instead of up to 10,000, so one large list no longer holds a server worker for seconds; the web app fetches full lists 1,000 rows at a time, and the interface and cable lists serialize 37-49% faster.
- #448 - **Tenant and prefix counts match what you can see.** A tenant's site, prefix, VLAN and IP counts, a tenant group's tenants, and a prefix's child prefix, IP, static-route and DNS counts now count only the rows you may view; in another tenant they count by your grants there.
- #449 - **Sign-in lockout holds under parallel requests.** Each password attempt is now counted before the password is checked, so at most 10 wrong passwords per client and account are tried in the window, even when sent in parallel.
- #438 - **More counts respect what you can see.** A tag's usage, a contact's or contact role's assignments, a custom-field group's fields, the circuits on a provider network, a cluster's or VM group's virtual machines, a location's and cabinet's devices, a floor plan's tiles, an L2VPN's VTEPs, a module type's interface templates and the sub-group counts now count only what the reader may view, so a site-scoped user's number matches the table under it.
- #445 - **Card lines label.** On the device form the Card lines heading no longer behaves as a label: clicking it no longer toggles Name only, and screen readers announce it as the name of the group.
- **Power tidy-ups.** Floor-plan tiles linked to a power panel or feed open its detail page instead of its edit form, the power panel and feed pages show the standard loading state, and `?cluster_site=` on the power panel list is ignored instead of failing with a server error.

### Dependencies

- vite 8.3.5, launch-editor 2.14.2 and follow-redirects 1.16.1 in the frontend's development tooling, clearing the open Dependabot advisories; none of the three ships in a running Danbyte.
